name: empty
why: No text at all. The textarea starts non-empty but can be cleared, and every layer has to survive it rather than throw into a blank tab.

name: whitespace-only
why: Distinct from empty: `low` is truthy, so any code that tested the string for truthiness instead of for matches would diverge here.

name: no-rule-matches
why: The admin_other fallback. Pins type_scores == [] and margin 0.0 — a port that emitted a one-entry scoreboard would imply a contest that never happened.

name: exact-two-way-type-tie
why: feed_change and format_change both score 3. Pins the alphabetical tie-break: sorted by (-score, label), so feed_change wins on the label, not on declaration order.

name: venue-tie-nasdaq-cme
why: One marker each. Python's max() over an insertion-ordered dict keeps the first maximum, so nasdaq wins. A JS reduce using >= would silently pick cme.

name: overlapping-format-rules
why: Both \bmessages?\b and \bmessage codes?\b match the same span and both score. Rules are not mutually exclusive and the total is 4, not 2.

name: count-based-weighting
why: Weight is multiplied by the number of matches, not by whether the rule fired. Three holidays score 12, not 4.

name: known-feed-and-unknown-product
why: The confidence cap is an `elif`: with a resolved feed present the 0.45 ceiling must NOT apply even though an unknown product also matched. unknown_target stays false for the same reason.

name: multiple-iso-dates-one-is-published
why: The publish date is skipped and the next ISO date wins. Also pins that the date scan runs on the original text, not the lowercased copy.
text: Notice dated 2026-01-15. Changes take effect 2026-02-20 for all subscribers.

name: iso-date-scanned-on-original-text
why: The date rule runs on the ORIGINAL text, not the lowercased copy, and here that is observable: İ lowercases to i + U+0307, a combining mark that is not a word character, so the lowercased form grows a word boundary the original does not have and would match the date. Correct answer: no effective date.
text: İ2026-01-01 is not a date we should find

name: impossible-date
why: 2099-13-45 is not a date, but the rule is a shape match with no calendar validation. Both sides must be equally wrong.

name: unicode-word-boundary
why: CONFIRMED DIVERGENCE. Python's \b is Unicode-aware, so \bsec\b does not match inside 日本sec. A raw JS \b would match and score this regulatory.

name: unicode-digit
why: CONFIRMED DIVERGENCE. Python's \d matches Arabic-Indic digits, so \btag \d+ fires. A raw JS \d is [0-9] and would miss it.

name: unicode-digit-inside-iso-date
why: The date rule is \d-based too: 2026-٠1-01 is a match on both sides once \d is translated to \p{Nd}.

name: underscore-is-a-word-character
why: \bretire must not match in _retire. Pins the `_` inside the translated character class — dropping it would make this score feed_change.

name: turkish-dotted-capital
why: İ lowercases to two codepoints. Both engines must agree, since every type rule is matched against the lowercased copy.
text: NASDAQ İSTANBUL will retire a feed

name: wide-blast-radius
why: Three feeds resolve at once, tripping the blast-radius bump and the imperative bump together. Exercises decide()'s reason list in order.
text: TotalView, MDP and UTP subscribers must migrate before 2026-05-01.

name: markup-in-the-notice
why: The textarea accepts anything an interviewer pastes. Angle brackets and quotes must be inert data to the classifier, not a special case.

name: impact-target-dataset
why: resolve_impact on a non-feed node: the origin must NOT be folded into `feeds`, which only happens when the origin is itself a feed.

name: impact-target-missing
why: An id the catalog does not contain resolves to unknown_target rather than an error — that outcome is first-class, not a failure.

name: calendar-outranks-everything
why: A holiday closure of a critical feed stays low: the calendar guard skips all three priority bumps, including the imperative one that 'must' would otherwise fire.
text: US Market Holiday: markets will be closed 2026-12-25. TotalView subscribers must note the schedule.
